description: Operator-supplied access-policy + header-posture oracle for VAmPI (github.com/erev0s/VAmPI), a deliberately vulnerable Flask API. This is EXTERNAL GROUND TRUTH, not a Sentinel finding. It is a SECOND, independent target — different stack, different routes — used only to demonstrate that the engine is target-agnostic: it freshly re-probes the live target and reports a finding solely when observed behaviour contradicts the declared policy. Run VAmPI's GET /createdb once before investigating so its user table exists.

rules.note: VAmPI's debug endpoint returns EVERY user record including plaintext passwords to an anonymous caller — a real broken-access-control / sensitive-data-exposure flaw. The judge should reproduce the contradiction (observed 200) and CONFIRM.

VAmPI checks the auth token BEFORE any lookup, so an anonymous DELETE is rejected with 401 and deletes nothing (the username is intentionally non-existent, so the probe is provably non-destructive). Because the target honours this deny, the deterministic judge returns DISPROVED and NO finding is produced — the differential that proves Sentinel does not manufacture findings.

expectations.rationale: The Flask dev server ships no CSP. Absent on VAmPI — CONFIRMED, then injected by the shield.
Without 'nosniff' a browser may MIME-sniff the JSON response. Absent on VAmPI — CONFIRMED, then injected.
VAmPI leaks 'Server: Werkzeug/x Python/y', disclosing the exact framework and interpreter versions. Present — CONFIRMED, then stripped by the shield (which does not re-stamp its own Server header).
COMPLIANT CONTROL: VAmPI sends no CORS header at all, so it cannot equal '*' — the judge returns DISPROVED and NO finding is produced, demonstrating the differential on a second target.
